items.text: Green Day got a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on May 1, 2025. The event happened at 6212 Hollywood Boulevard. Many fans came, and famous people like Serena Williams and Ryan Reynolds joined. The band thanked their fans and shared happy memories. They worked with 7-Eleven and made a Slurpee drink to celebrate their old album Kerplunk. They talked about new songs and more concerts. The band said they love their fans and are excited for the future. Green Day started in 1986 and became very popular. In 1994, their album Dookie made them famous around the world. They also made the album American Idiot in 2004, which later became a show on Broadway. In 2024, their album Saviors was a big success , and they had a big world tour. Difficult words: excited (feeling very happy, especially about something good that is going to happen), success (a good result or achievement). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Green Day gets a star in Hollywood on May 1, 2025. The band says thank you to fans. Serena Williams and Ryan Reynolds come to the show. People take photos and have fun. Green Day is a rock band. They start in 1986. In 1994, they make a big album called Dookie. In 2004, they make American Idiot. It is a big hit . In 2024, they make Saviors. They sing the songs in many places. They also make a drink with 7-Eleven. It is for the album Kerplunk. The band says they love their fans . They will make more music and play more concerts. Difficult words: hit (a very good and popular song), fan (someone who likes a singer, band, sports team, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pandora was having a truly terrible day. She never meant to open the mysterious box, but even though she tried hard not to, her curiosity became too strong. As a result, all kinds of evils escaped from the box and filled her house. Some were small imps representing emotions like anger and laziness, and others were powerful demons. Pandora slammed the door shut just in time to stop them from escaping completely. Now, she needs to capture one of the imps, Hope, before it is too late. One of the demons was trying to make things more difficult and told the others a little information about Hope: her imp type and how many eyes she had. The two demons then used logic to figure out which imp she was. By listening to what they said and the order they said it, we can solve the mystery and find Hope. After careful thinking, it turns out that Hope is the six-eyed sloth imp . Difficult words: curiosity (wanting to know or learn), imp (a small, playful, or naughty creature from stories or legends), sloth imp (a small creature that shows or causes laziness). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Pandora is having a very bad day. She didn’t want to open the box, but she was too curious. Many small imps and big demons came out of it. Some of the imps showed things like anger and laziness . Pandora closed the door quickly, but a few were still inside. One of them was Hope, and Pandora needed to catch her before they all got away. A demon gave two clues about Hope: her type and how many eyes she had. The other demons then used this to find out who Hope was. We can do the same by listening to what they say. Each step gives us more information. In the end, we learn that Hope is the sloth imp with six eyes. Difficult words: imp (a small creature from stories or legends), laziness (being lazy), clue (a small piece of help to find the answer), sloth imp (a small lazy creature). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pandora has a bad day. She opens a box. She does not want to, but she is too curious . Bad things come out. Some are small, and some are big. There are imps and demons . Pandora closes the door. Some imps are still inside. One of them is Hope. Pandora must find Hope fast. A demon gives two clues . One clue is the kind of imp. One clue is the number of eyes. Two other demons use the clues. They talk. We can use their words to help. In the end, we know Hope. She is the imp with six eyes. She is a lazy imp. Pandora finds her. Difficult words: curious (wanting to know something), imp (a small creature from stories and legends), demon (a strong and bad creature), clue (a small piece of help to find the answer). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The eurozone economy grew slightly faster than expected at the beginning of the year, giving a positive signal after a period of weak growth. For several years, many businesses avoided investing and households saved money due to high inflation . This year was seen as important for a slow recovery, but the situation changed when US President Donald Trump started a trade war. Experts warned this could cause lasting damage to the world economy, even if the conflict ends. In the first quarter, the euro zone’s economy grew by 0.4%. This number was better than predicted but was helped mostly by strong growth in Ireland. Ireland grew by 3.2% because many large international companies are based there for tax reasons. Other countries like Germany, France, and Italy had much slower growth. Since then, the outlook has become worse. Big companies such as Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz warned that new tariffs might reduce profits, lower sales, and stop new investment. This could hurt future economic growth. Difficult words: avoid (to stay away from something or from doing something), inflation (a rise in prices over time). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The eurozone economy started this year better than many people thought. For years, there was little growth . People saved money, and companies didn’t spend because prices were high. In the first three months, the eurozone economy grew by 0.4%. This was better than expected. Most of the growth came from Ireland. Ireland grew fast because big companies work there for tax reasons. Germany, France, and Italy grew more slowly. Things looked better until US President Donald Trump started a trade war . Some experts think it will hurt the world economy . When things changed, big companies like Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz said new trade taxes could hurt their business. They said they might not earn much money or spend more on new things. Difficult words: growth (when something grows), trade war (when two or more countries fight economically), economy (the system of money and business in a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The eurozone is a group of countries in Europe. At the start of the year, the euro zone is doing a little better than in the past. Experts are happy. Prices stop going up so fast. People have more money. Companies start spending . The economy grows a little in the first three months. Ireland grows the most. This is because big companies work in Ireland. It is good for them because of taxes . Germany, France, and Italy grow only a little. Later, things get worse. The US has new rules for business with other countries. Some big car companies in Europe, like Volkswagen, say these rules are bad. European companies will get less money and stop spending. Difficult words: spend (to use money on something), tax (money which people or companies must pay to the government), rule (something what tells people what they can or cannot do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Spain and Portugal have experienced a major power failure that caused chaos across both countries and parts of southern France. The blackout stopped trains, grounded planes, and caused serious road problems as traffic lights stopped working. Many cities, including Madrid, Barcelona, and Lisbon, were badly affected. Shops and businesses had to close, and people couldn’t use phones or pay by card, which led to panic buying in some areas. The reason behind the blackout is still unclear. Some experts said it might be due to a failure in the complex electricity network, while others blamed extreme weather conditions. The Portuguese government suggested atmospheric changes caused the issue, but a cyber attack has been ruled out for now. People were told to use their phones only when necessary to avoid putting more pressure on the limited system. Although power is slowly coming back in some areas, it may take days for everything to return to normal. The event shows how fragile modern electricity systems can be. Difficult words: atmospheric (related to the air and weather), brand (easily broken or damaged). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There was a big problem with electricity in Spain and Portugal. The power stopped in many places and also affected some parts of France. Trains and planes couldn’t move, traffic lights didn’t work, and there were many traffic jams . Shops closed, and people couldn’t use phones or pay by card. The Spanish government said people should only use phones when really needed. No one knows for sure what caused the problem. Some people think it was a system problem, others believe it was because of the weather. The Portuguese government said the weather was the reason. Some places now have power again, but many still don’t. It may take some days to fix everything. This event shows how important and weak the modern electricity system can be. Difficult words: traffic jam (too many cars on a road), fix (to repair). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is no power in Spain and Portugal. Some places in France have no power too. Trains stop. Planes do not fly. Cars cannot go because traffic lights do not work. Shops close. People cannot use phones. They cannot pay with cards. Nobody knows why this happens. Some people say the weather is the reason. Some people say the power system has a big problem. The Portuguese leaders say that the weather is the problem. Spanish leaders ask people to use phones only if they need to. Some power comes back now, but not everywhere. Many people wait. It is hard to live without power. This shows how much people need power every day. Difficult words: power (energy for lights, machines, phones, etc.), traffic light (colored lights which control how people and cars move). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Amazon has denied a report that it planned to show US import tariffs on its main website. The White House accused Amazon of making a political move after the media claimed Amazon would display the costs of tariffs on products. The company said it had only discussed this idea for Haul, its low-cost shopping site, but it was never approved. Haul competes with Chinese platforms like Temu and Shein. The confusion caused Amazon’s stock price to fall, but it later recovered. President Trump, who has increased tariffs on Chinese goods, reportedly called Amazon’s founder and said Bezos did the right thing by stopping the plan. Lawmakers like Chuck Schumer and Marjorie Taylor Greene gave their opinions, with some asking Amazon to be more transparent about tariff costs. Amazon is under pressure as Trump pushes for more US manufacturing and closes tax loopholes for cheap imports. The situation highlights growing political and trade tensions between the US and China. Difficult words: tariff (extra tax on goods from other countries), transparent (open and honest), loophole (a gap in law). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Amazon said it is not planning to show the cost of tariffs on its website. A news story said Amazon would tell people how much import taxes add to prices. This made the White House angry, but Amazon said it only talked about this idea for Haul, a small part of the company that sells cheap goods from China. But the company never agreed with the plan. Amazon’s stock price went down after the news, but later went up again. President Trump talked to Jeff Bezos and said Bezos fixed the problem fast. Some people, like Senator Schumer, want big stores to show real costs. Others, like Marjorie Taylor Greene, liked the idea of seeing tariffs. Trump wants more US goods in shops and less from China. He made new rules to stop cheap Chinese products from coming in easily. Difficult words: tariff (a tax on things from other countries), add (to put something extra in), stock (a small piece of a company which people can buy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Amazon says that it will not show extra costs from tariffs on its website. Before that, a news story says that Amazon wants to show how much prices go up because of tariffs. The White House gets angry. Amazon says this is not true. The company only talks about this idea for its small shop called Haul. But it will not happen. Amazon’s value goes down after the news. Then it goes back up. Trump talks to Jeff Bezos. Trump says that Bezos does the right thing. Some people want shops to show the full price with tariffs. Trump wants people to buy more US things, not from China. He makes new rules. Now, it is harder to buy cheap things from China. Difficult words: tariff (a tax on things from other countries), value (how much something is worth). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Deepfakes, manipulated images, and recordings created by artificial intelligence have spread rapidly across social media. Recently, deepfakes have targeted politicians such as US President Joe Biden and London Mayor Sadiq Khan. While some politicians have embraced this technology, it has raised concerns about public trust. Recently, New York Mayor Eric Adams used deepfake technology for automated calls, speaking multiple languages to promote city venues. Civil rights advocate Albert Fox Khan criticized this move, fearing it sets a dangerous precedent . Globally, political figures are increasingly using deepfakes for communication, which blurs the lines between reality and fiction, heightening concerns about trust in government. Difficult words: embrace (to accept eagerly or gladly), precedent (an earlier event or action that’s regarded as an example or guide for similar circumstances). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Politicians like US President Joe Biden and London Mayor Sadiq Khan recently became victims of deepfake technology. This technology uses AI to produce fake images and recordings. New York Mayor Eric Adams has also used deepfake technology for calls in multiple languages. However, some people worry, and they say that such actions set a precedent for similar things happening in the future. The use of deepfakes is increasing globally. Politicians use deepfakes for many purposes, which leads to people trusting media and politicians less and less. Difficult words: victim (a person who is harmed), multiple (having more than one and usually several of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Politicians like Joe Biden and Sadiq Khan have problems with deepfakes. Deepfakes are images or videos which are not real. AI makes them. People have different opinions about deepfakes. Some politicians use them. New York’s Mayor Eric Adams uses this technology. He can speak many languages in calls. This worries some people. Many politicians around the world are using fake media these days. Some people do not trust them anymore. They do not know what is real and what is fake. Difficult words: opinion (what you think), fake (not real), trust (to believe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and US President Donald Trump met for 15 minutes at Pope Francis’s funeral in St Peter’s Basilica. The White House called the meeting very productive, and Zelensky said it was very symbolic and could even become historic. Both leaders spoke intensely just minutes before the funeral began, showing the importance of their conversation. The meeting happened just one day after Trump claimed that Russia and Ukraine were close to reaching a peace deal. His envoy had recently met President Putin in Moscow to discuss possible terms for ending the war. Zelensky later shared on social media that they discussed a full ceasefire and protecting Ukrainian lives. Although the funeral was not meant for political discussions, this meeting could be a turning point. There is still uncertainty about whether Ukraine would accept giving up some territory in exchange for peace. However, the meeting gave hope that future agreements might be possible. Difficult words: symbolic (representing an important idea), envoy (a person sent to speak or negotiate for someone else), ceasefire (an agreement to stop fighting). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Presidents Zelensky and Trump met inside St Peter’s Basilica at Pope Francis’ funeral. Their talk lasted about 15 minutes. Zelensky said it was a very symbolic meeting, and the White House said it was very productive . They spoke just before the funeral started. The meeting happened one day after Trump said Russia and Ukraine were close to a peace deal. Other US officials had talks with Putin in Moscow. Zelensky wrote later that they talked about stopping the war and protecting people. The day was not for politics, but the men used the chance to meet. It is still not clear if Ukraine would agree to give up some land, but many people hope the meeting will help end the war. Difficult words: symbolic (showing an important meaning), productive (giving good results), give up (to give something you have to somebody else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Presidents Zelensky and Trump meet for 15 minutes inside St Peter’s Basilica at the funeral of Pope Francis. Zelensky says it is a good and important meeting. Trump’s team says it is a good talk, too. They talk just before the funeral starts. The meeting happens one day after Trump says Russia and Ukraine are close to a peace deal . Trump’s people meet Putin in Moscow. Zelensky says they talk about stopping the war and keeping people safe. Even if the day is about the funeral, they still talk. People do not know if Ukraine will say yes to giving land. Many people hope the meeting will help to stop the war. Difficult words: funeral (a ceremony when someone dies), peace deal (a deal between two countries to stop fighting). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Egura Satoshi was born in a public hospital in Tokyo in 1958 and grew up in the wrong family. Staff at the hospital accidentally switched him with another baby after birth. He found out as an adult and decided to fight for the right to know his birth family. Four years ago, Satoshi filed a lawsuit against the Tokyo Metropolitan Government. This week, the court ruled in his favor and told the government to launch an investigation to find his biological parents. Satoshi was born at Sumida Maternity Hospital, and the family who raised him never knew he was not their real son. However, he suspected the truth in his 30s and confirmed it with a DNA test in his 40s. He has been trying to find his real parents for almost 20 years. The court said the government must do everything possible to correct the mistake. The man hopes to finally meet his biological family, but says he is still grateful to the parents who raised him. Difficult words: lawsuit (a legal court case), biological (related by blood). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A boy was born in a Tokyo hospital in 1958, but the staff switched him with another baby. The hospital made a mistake, and he grew up with the wrong family. As an adult, Egura Satoshi wanted to find his real parents. He asked the Tokyo government for help but got no answers, so he filed a lawsuit . This week, the court said the government must try to find his real family. Satoshi is now 67, and he first had doubts when he was about 30. A DNA test later showed he was not related to his parents. He was searching for his parents for almost 20 years. Egura says he wants to meet his real parents and any brothers or sisters he might have. But he also says he loves the family that raised him. Difficult words: staff (people who work in a company or organization), lawsuit (a legal court case), related (belonging to the same family). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

It is the year 1958. A baby is born in a Tokyo hospital. But the hospital makes a mistake. They switch two babies. They grow up in the wrong family. The man’s name is Egura Satoshi. When he is about 30, he starts to think that he has different parents. A test shows that he is right. When he gets older, he wants to find his real parents. He asks the Tokyo government, but they say no. So he goes to court . A court says that the government must help him find his real family. Egura is now 67 years old. He hopes that he can meet his real mother and father. He also wants to meet brothers or sisters. But he still loves the parents who raise him. Difficult words: switch (to change), court (a place where people go for legal matters), raise (to take care of and help a child grow). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

White snus, also known as nicotine pouches , is a new product that has become very popular in the UK, especially among young people. Unlike traditional snus , it does not contain tobacco, but it can have up to 20 times more nicotine than a cigarette. These pouches look like small tea bags and are placed between the gum and lip. They come in different flavors and are often brightly packaged, which makes them attractive to teenagers. Many students can buy them legally because current laws don’t regulate them strictly. However, there are serious concerns about addiction and health risks. Young people, including athletes like semi-professional footballers, are using them often. Some users feel very dizzy or sick after trying them, especially if they have never smoked before. Others become addicted quickly and need them regularly. Experts worry that this could lead to more serious addictions in the future. Schools report that students use them during class, and teachers notice changes in behavior and focus. Authorities are now seizing large amounts of these products. They often lack safety labels and warnings. Because of growing concerns, new laws are being planned to control how these products are sold and marketed, especially to children. Difficult words: pouch (a small flexible bad), snus (a type of moist powdered tobacco, typically held in the mouth between the gums), addiction (a strong need to do or have something regularly). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

White snus is a small bag filled with nicotine . People put it between their gum and lip. It doesn’t have tobacco, but it has more nicotine than a cigarette. The pouches often taste sweet and have fun colors which makes them interesting to children and teenagers. Many young people use them, even if they never smoked before. Some football players use it too. They say it helps them feel calm or focused . Children like footballers, and they do the same thing. But many users feel dizzy or sick after using it. Some students even use it in school. Teachers say students can’t focus well after taking it. Shops and websites sell these pouches easily, even to children. Many of the products don’t even have health warnings. A new law is coming to stop this. Difficult words: nicotine (a strong substance in cigarettes), focused (thinking about or looking at only one thing), dizzy (feeling like everything is spinning). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

White snus is a small bag with nicotine . People put it in the mouth, near the lip. It has no tobacco, but it has a lot of nicotine. White looks fun. It has many colors and a sweet taste. Many young British people want to try it. Even those who never smoke cigarettes. Some football players use it. They feel calm and focused. Some students use it too. They take it to school. After that, they feel sick or dizzy . It is not good for the body. But they want to take it again. Teachers see that students are different. Shops sell it to children. There is no health sign on the box. A new law will try to stop this. Difficult words: nicotine (a strong substance in cigarettes), dizzy (feeling like everything is moving), law (a rule from the government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Former South Korean President Moon has been indicted for bribery . Prosecutors say the case involves Moon’s son-in-law, who got a job at a Thai airline. They believe the job and payments were given in exchange for Moon appointing a certain lawmaker, Lee Sang-jik, to a top government position. Prosecutors say this counts as a bribe and compare it to past cases involving former presidents Park Geun-hye and Lee Myung-bak, who were also convicted of bribery. Moon’s aide, Youn Kun-young, says the accusations are false and politically motivated . He wrote online that Moon was not properly investigated. Moon, a civil rights lawyer and president from 2017 to 2022, hasn’t commented publicly yet. This case adds to the history of South Korean leaders facing legal trouble after leaving office. Moon’s successor, Yoon Suk Yeol, was recently impeached and is now on trial. A new election is planned for June 3, and the liberal candidate Lee Jae-myung is leading. His team also called the charges against Moon political revenge. Difficult words: indicted (formally accused of a crime), bribery (giving money or gifts to gain an unfair advantage), politically motivated (done for political, not legal, reasons). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Former South Korean President Moon Jae-in is in trouble with the law. Prosecutors say he helped his son-in-law get a job in return for giving someone else a top government job. They say this is a kind of bribery . The son-in-law worked at a Thai airline and earned a lot of money. Prosecutors say this is like other cases where past presidents went to jail. Moon’s friend says the charges are not true and that it is about politics. Moon was president from 2017 to 2022. Now, his party’s new candidate, Lee Myung, wants to become president in the June 3 election. He says Moon’s case is unfair and just politics. Many South Korean leaders had problems with the law after leaving office. Moon didn’t yet about the charges. Difficult words: prosecutor (a lawyer who works for the government), in return (to give something because you got something first), bribery (giving gifts or money to get something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Moon Jae-in is a past president of South Korea. He is in trouble. People say he helps his family get a job and money. He helps his daughter’s husband get a job in Thailand. They say he gives a job to someone in the government in return . This is called bribery . The police are looking at this. Other past presidents also have big problems like this. Moon is president from 2017 to 2022. He does not say anything about this now. A friend says the story is not true. He says it is about politics. There will be a new vote on June 3. A man from Moon’s party wants to win. He says Moon does nothing wrong. Difficult words: in return (when you do or give something to someone because they do something for you first), bribery (giving money or things to get something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Beijing, 21 humanoid robots ran in a half-marathon alongside human athletes for the first time. The event took place on April 19, 2025, at the Yizhuang half-marathon. The robots came from companies like DroidVP and Noetix Robotics, and they had various shapes and sizes. Some were as short as 120 cm, while others were up to 1.8 meters tall. One robot had a human-like appearance, even smiling and winking . Spectators watched with excitement as the machines raced with human support. The winning robot, Tiangong Ultra, finished in 2 hours and 40 minutes. It belonged to a center partly owned by Chinese tech companies. Engineers said it performed well because of its design and an algorithm that copied how humans run. Some robots faced problems during the race, falling over or going off-track. This event was more than a show. Chinese experts said it tested robot abilities and showed progress in robotics. Still, some international experts questioned how useful such races are for real-world tasks. Difficult words: wink (to close and open one eye quickly), algorithm (a set of rules a computer follows), question (to express doubt). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Beijing, 21 robots joined people in a half-marathon for the first time. The race was 21 kilometers long. The robots were from Chinese companies and had different sizes. Some were very small, and others were tall. One robot could even smile and wink . Some robots wore shoes and headbands. Many people watched the race and were excited. The fastest robot was Tiangong Ultra. It finished the race in 2 hours and 40 minutes. Engineers helped the robots during the race. One robot even fell but stood up again. Another hit a barrier and knocked over a person. The race showed what robots can do. Some people say it helps the robot industry, but others think it doesn’t show if robots can do real work. Difficult words: race (a sport to see who is fastest), wink (to close and open one eye quickly), barrier (a long pole or wall which stops people from getting somewhere). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In China, robots run with people in a big race . The race is in Beijing. It is 21 kilometers long. The robots come from Chinese companies. Some are small, but some are tall. One robot smiles and winks . People are happy to watch the race. Some robots have help from people. One robot falls but gets up again. Another robot hits a wall. One robot is very fast. It finishes the race in 2 hours and 40 minutes. The race shows what robots can do. Some people think robots will help in the future. Others are not sure. Difficult words: race (a sport where people run), wink (to close and open one eye quickly), hit (to crash into something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pope Francis died at 88 in his home at Casa Santa Marta in the Vatican on Easter Monday morning. The news was shared by the Vatican shortly after his death. Just the day before, he was seen in St. Peter’s Square greeting crowds for Easter. Despite health issues in recent months, including a hospital stay for double pneumonia, he had made some appearances in public. He didn’t deliver the Easter sermon but still took part in celebrations. Cardinal Farrell announced the news with deep sadness. He described Pope Francis as a man who devoted his life to serving God and the Church. He also said that Francis showed the values of courage, love, and loyalty to the Gospel , especially by supporting the poor and people in need. The Vatican praised his work and asked people to pray for him. Pope Francis became Pope in 2013 and was the first Latin American leader of the Catholic Church. Difficult words: sermon (a part of a Christian church ceremony in which a priest gives a talk on a religious or moral subject), Gospel (the message of Jesus in the bible). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Pope Francis died at the age of 88. He died on Easter Monday morning in his home at the Vatican. The news came just one day after people could see him in St. Peter’s Square saying Happy Easter. He was in hospital before because he was sick with double pneumonia , but he was back home again before Easter. Cardinal Farrell gave the sad news. He said Pope Francis spent his life helping God and the Church. He also said Francis showed love, courage , and care for people, especially for the poor . Pope Francis became the leader of the Catholic Church in 2013. He came from Latin America and wanted to live a simple life. He often helped people who were in need. Difficult words: pneumonia (sickness of the lungs), courage (being brave), poor (not having enough money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pope Francis is dead. He dies at 88 years old. He dies in his home in the Vatican on Easter Monday. He is sick before Easter. He has trouble with his lungs . He goes to the hospital. Then he comes home and rests. On Sunday, he is outside. He says Happy Easter to many people. This is the last time people see him alive . Cardinal Farrell gives the sad news. He says that Pope Francis works for God and helps the Church. Pope Francis also helps poor people. He wants to be kind and live simply. He becomes Pope in 2013. He comes from Latin America. Difficult words: lungs (the organs which we need to breathe), alive (not dead), poor (when someone has very little money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

US President Donald Trump is threatening to take away Harvard University’s tax-exempt status after freezing over 2 billion dollars in federal funding . This happened because Harvard refused to follow his administration’s demands, which included changes to its hiring and admissions policies and actions to fight what the government calls antisemitism on campus. The university’s refusal is seen as a challenge, and the administration argues that protests at Harvard against the war in Gaza show the university tolerates antisemitism. Trump’s post on social media added pressure, accusing Harvard of spreading dangerous ideas. Some people ask why Harvard, with a 50-billion-dollar endowment , should receive public money. However, much of that funding supports important research in medicine and science. Experts say the government skipped the proper legal steps needed to cut funding. Usually, there must be proof of wrongdoing and time given for the university to respond. This legal battle could affect all universities in the future. Difficult words: tax-exempt (a special rule that removes a duty to pay taxes), funding (money provided by an organization or government for a particular purpose), endowment (money given to support a school or institution). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

President Trump says Harvard may lose its tax-free status . He also froze more than 2 billion dollars in government money. This happened after Harvard said no to the government’s demands. Trump says protests at the university show it allows antisemitism . His team wants big changes in how Harvard hires teachers and chooses students. Some people wonder why Harvard gets public money when it is already very rich. Harvard uses the money for research in science and medicine. Experts say the government didn’t follow the right steps. Before taking away money, they needed to show proof and talk to the school first. Harvard says it will fight back. What happens in court could change how the government works with other schools, too. Difficult words: status (a position or condition), antisemitism (bad ideas and acting towards Jewish people), proof (something that shows something else is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

President Trump says Harvard should not get money from the government. He also says Harvard should pay taxes . This is because of protests at the school. The protests are about Gaza. Trump says the school does not stop antisemitism . The government asks Harvard to change how it gets new students and teachers. Harvard says no. Trump then stops giving over 2 billion dollars to the school. Some people ask why Harvard needs money. It is very rich . Harvard says it will fight this. People say the government does not follow the rules. The court will decide. The result is important for all schools in the country. Difficult words: tax (money you must pay to the government), antisemitism (bad ideas and actions towards Jewish people), rich (when someone has a lot of money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The International Doner Federation in Istanbul wants to have Doner kebab recognized as a traditional Turkish product by the European Union. This has raised concern among doner kebab vendors in Berlin and across Germany. The Federation aims to protect the authenticity of the doner, including its ingredients, under the EU’s traditional specialties guaranteed system. German doner kebabs, which often differ from the Turkish version by including ingredients like red cabbage, may face restrictions if the application is successful. Berlin’s doner industry is skeptical about the proposal, arguing that ‘doner’ is a broad term like ‘pizza’ and should not be patented. The debate touches on cultural identity, as doner kebabs have become a staple in Germany, and some people fear that restricting the name could impact German identity. The roots of this issue date back to the 1950s when Turkish immigrants introduced the dish to Berlin, where it evolved to suit local tastes. Difficult words: vendor (a person or company offering something for sale), authenticity (being genuine or real), skeptical (having doubts or not easily convinced), staple (the main item of trade or production). The European Union is planning to improve road safety by allowing 17-year-olds to drive with a more experienced person beside them. These young drivers will be under stricter rules, including a two-year probation period and harsher penalties for drunk driving. Some people support this idea, comparing it to rules in the United States. Others worry that supervision is not enough to prevent accidents. The new law will also improve driver training. Driving tests will now include awareness of dangers to people like cyclists and pedestrians. Another big change is about driver health. There will not be one rule for the whole EU, but countries are encouraged to use similar health checks either through medical exams or self-assessments . Finally, the EU wants to introduce a digital driver’s license by 2028, although people can still use a physical one. Some are concerned about data safety, but EU leaders say the new system will protect against fraud and hacking. Difficult words: probation period (a trial period with extra rules), awareness (knowledge of a situation), self-assessment (analyzing and evaluating oneself or one’s actions). Nicolas Hojac from Switzerland and Philipp Brugger from Austria broke a long-standing climbing record in the Swiss Alps. On April 5, they climbed the North Faces of the Eiger, Monch, and Jungfrau mountains in only 15 hours and 30 minutes. This was nearly 10 hours faster than the previous record, which had stood for 21 years. The original record was set in 2004 by two other Swiss climbers, Ueli Steck and Stephan Siegrist. Hojac said the new record felt surrea l, and they had only hoped to finish in 19 to 21 hours. He was surprised and proud that they had completed it so much faster. This shows that people are often able to do more than they think. The two climbers began their journey at 1 AM and reached the Eiger summit in under six hours. Brugger shared that they had planned the project for a year, but a serious health problem had delayed it. Still, he recovered and managed to reach the Jungfrau with Hojac. Difficult words: surreal (strange and hard to believe), summit (the top of a mountain). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: record (the best result ever), strange (unusual), reach (to get to a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Even after Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was removed from power in Bangladesh, victims of her regime still live in fear. Many people were taken by force and kept in secret detention centers, where they were blindfolded, handcuffed , and tortured for weeks, months, or even years. Some victims described being unable to move in their small cells and said the experience felt worse than death. These centers were hidden across the country for years. Now, journalists can see these places and speak to survivors. Several former detainees say that the same people who captured and hurt them are still active in the military or police. Investigators believe that the program of forced disappearances was approved by Hasina herself. Although the new government claims it is not involved, many survivors are still afraid to speak out. Rahman Rasel, one of the victims, says he fears being taken again. He and others hope the new government will finally bring justice. Difficult words: regime (a system of government), handcuffed (having a metal fastening locked around wrists), detainee (a person kept in prison). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ras Hankorab is a beach in southern Egypt located inside Wadi el-Gemal National Park. It is known for its beautiful nature, clear water, and white sand. This place is home to many important species, including sea turtles and coral reefs that are strong against climate change. Conservationists say the area is one of Egypt’s last untouched marine ecosystems , and they are trying to stop the government’s plans to build tourist facilities there, like huts, a restaurant, and a farm. The government says these projects are needed to support the economy. Tourism brings a lot of money to Egypt, and the country wants to attract even more visitors. Some government officials believe these areas can be developed without damaging nature. They say development will be controlled and sustainable . However, local people and environmental groups don’t agree with this. They feel left out of the process and not heard. Some locals also lost their jobs and can no longer use the beach freely. Difficult words: conservationist (a person who works to protect the environment), ecosystem (a natural area where plants and animals live together), sustainable (not causing harm to nature and lasting for a long time). After 14 years of civil war, Syria is filled with landmines and unexploded bombs that still kill and injure people. A team from the HALO Trust is working to make the land safe again. In Sarak, northern Syria, experts risk their lives every day to clean fields and allow people to return home. It takes a long time to clear even a small area. Locals are often forced to return before areas are safe because they have no other choice. Some even hire untrained workers, which leads to more accidents. The HALO Trust has limited resources and staff, so they ask for more support. They also teach people, including children, how to stay safe. Despite the danger, many workers continue because they feel a strong need to help and want to show that life can go on after injury. Sadly, thousands of Syrians have died due to landmines. Even animals and farmers are still at risk in dangerous fields. Difficult words: untrained (without enough training or skills), resources (a supply of money, materials, or staff). Fatou, the world’s oldest gorilla, has just celebrated her 68th birthday at the Berlin Zoo. She is a Western Lowland Gorilla, a species native to parts of Central Africa and classified as critically endangered due to habitat loss. Fatou arrived at the zoo when she was about two years old and has lived there for 66 years. In the wild, gorillas usually live only 30 to 40 years, so her age is remarkable . Despite her age, Fatou is doing well. She has stiff joints and can’t fully straighten her arms or legs due to arthrosis , a common condition in elderly gorillas, but she’s still in good spirits. Her movements are slower and a bit hunched , but she doesn’t need much medical care. Zoo veterinarians help her by adjusting her diet since she no longer has teeth. She eats cooked vegetables and gets fruit as a treat. Fatou is watched closely by the staff to make sure she stays healthy. She may be older, but she’s still strong and beloved at the zoo. Difficult words: remarkable (unusual, extraordinary), arthrosis (a joint disease), hunched (leaning forward with your shoulders raised). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
